title: They just fixed MCP...
description:
Finally, MCP is now stateless - as it should have been from the start.

#softwaredevelopment #aidevelopment #mcp
transcript:
Finally, MCP is now stateless - as it should have been from the start.

top_comments.author: @propavangameryt405
top_comments.text: They are fighting with MCP instead of just using REST APIs, anyway the models are already intelligent enough to understand the response and request of an API why don’t we just use openAPI spec and just move on as usual instead bringing this new protocol and fixing the same things that engineers have solved ages ago..! 😅

top_reply.author: @somark28
top_reply.text: Its just an AI-native wrapper. I prefer it because there's less deviation where a model has to understand the specifics of the request being made, more abstraction is better in this case

top_comments.author: @TheCustomFHD
top_comments.text: And it also increases network load. Great idea.

top_comments.author: @nesssel
top_comments.text: Huh, wasn't all of this was possible before. At this point the spec has changed so often and so drastically that they'd be better off just making a new protocol or find a clean mapping from Stdio to HTTP to take all the features from HTTP directly instead of copying them.

top_comments.author: @daveinpublic
top_comments.text: You’re always shaking your head and raising and lowering your eyebrows and raising and lowering your shoulders and smiling and moving your hands back and forth constantly and at the same time. Just thought it was interesting.

top_reply.author: @JamesJosephFinn
top_reply.text: It’s hard balancing a big brain, you wouldn’t understand.

top_comments.author: @teamerx
top_comments.text: MCPs never were stateful. .. thier implementations were and that is the fault of whoever implemented them.. session pinning is there since ages. just use openAPI schemas ffs

top_comments.author: @br3nto
top_comments.text:
Stop pushing and encouraging MCP. Let it die. It’s an unnecessary abstraction that only adds complexity and an additional unneeded layer over your APIs and scripts.

If you use MCP, I encourage you to simply delete the MCP and see if you can get the same results simply using skills. I bet you can. The skill merely needs to describe the API, and provide a url to the docs, like swagger.

top_comments.author: @kennethjevans
top_comments.text: Vibe coders don't know what any of this means and real devs DGAF. Who cares.

top_reply.author: @end.0003
top_reply.text: The vibe coders discovered "we can give agents APIs but give it a fancy name"
